Jacqueline Scholl 2024, based on Legrand 2022 (and their R code)

Note: to preprocess the heart rate signal, i.e. look for outliers, we used the systole package from Legrand and Allen (2022) in Python and upload the results here.

# Packages, loading
Load the raw data, but also the pre-processed data, so that we can compare our and their results

Data columns:

- Condition: 'Less' or 'More',refers to response BPM being smaller than ('less') listenBPM
- Modality: Extero or Intero, refers to two task conditoins, comparing either the heart beat or external sounds
- Decision: 'Less' or 'More', refers to participants ratings
- DecisionRT
- Confidence: rating of confidence in the response
- ConfidenceRT
- ResponseCorrect: whether Decision and Condition match
- listenBPM and responseBPM: the beats per minute of the sound/heart in the 'listening' and 'comparing' intervals


Columns with only the sae entry for each:
- TrialType?? all are 'psi'
- StairCond, all 'psi'

From their model?:
- Alpha
- EstimatedThreshold
- EstimatedSlope

From the paper:
- rejecting trials with responses < 100ms
- rejecting trials with 'unreliable heartbeat signal', i.e. absolute deviation around the median rule (Leys et al. 2013), i.e. outliers in average heart rate or standard deviation of pulse-to-pulse interval an outlier

In the code from the original paper, they're R files are in docs>source>examples>R

# Control analyses - mean heart rate
In theory the meditation interventions (or order) could have changed the overall heart rate mean. Given that this was in fact the case, we later perform control regressions (i.e. including mean heart rate as an individual difference effect). 
It is also possible (though it wasn't the case) that it could have changed heart rate variability. This could have been particularly problematic from a technical point of view because it changes the range of regressors. 

JS 10/6/2025: detected a mistake in computing the heart rates - we did not filter by Modality and in the exteroception, that is the sound not the heart rate. This is fixed now, need to redo tables in the paper.
```{r}
heart.rates.mean.sd= cardio %>% 
  dplyr::filter(Modality=='Intero') %>% group_by(ID,session,order) %>% 
  dplyr::summarize(listenBPM.mean=mean(listenBPM),
                   listenBPM.sd  = sd(listenBPM)) %>% 
  pivot_wider(.,id_cols=c('ID','order'),names_from='session',values_from=c('listenBPM.mean','listenBPM.sd')) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(heartRate.mean_cdm_min_ndm = listenBPM.mean_CDM-listenBPM.mean_NDM,
                heartRate.sd_cdm_min_ndm = listenBPM.sd_CDM-listenBPM.sd_NDM)

lm.heartrate.mean=lm(heartRate.mean_cdm_min_ndm~ 1+order,data=heart.rates.mean.sd)
lm.heartrate.sd=lm(heartRate.sd_cdm_min_ndm~ 1+order,data=heart.rates.mean.sd)
sink(file.path(paths$stats,'HeartRate_session_meansSds_regressions.txt'))
summary(lm.heartrate.mean)
summary(lm.heartrate.sd)
print('mean heart rates and sds')
sink()
write.csv(heart.rates.mean.sd %>% dplyr::ungroup() %>% dplyr::summarize_if(is.numeric,mean),file=file.path(paths$stats,'HeartRate_session_meansSds.csv'))

                                                     
```



# Fit models for each person, for each session, for each condition:
- choice (more/less) ~ stimulus difficulty + ? stimulus per se + ? response repetition bias?
- confidence: they have the relationship between confidence and ground truth accuracy


Key models for the paper: choice and confidence
##Fit
Note that the scaling was done across all subjects, on an ungrouped data frame, not within each person.This makes sense because the task difficulty was individually adjusted, so z-scoring within each person could have removed individual differences we are interested in.

Control analyses:
- includ mean(heart+sound)
- heart and sound separately
- basic, non-zscored (for plotting)
- for log likelihoods: use non-zscored
```{r}
results.indivModalities=data.frame()
results.indivModalities.notScaled.forPlot=data.frame()
results.logLiks = data.frame()

cardio.scaled=cardio %>% dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate_at(vars(c('DV_ResponseMinListen','easiness_ResponseMinListen.abs','DecisionRT','Confidence',
                          'listenBPM','listen.responseBPM.mean','responseBPM','rollingHeartAvg.5tr','rollingResponseAvg.5tr.prev')),scale)
for (isub in unique(cardio$ID)){
  dft=cardio.scaled %>% dplyr::filter(ID==isub) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Decision = dplyr::recode(Decision,'More'=1,'Less'=0))
  dft.nonScaled=cardio %>% dplyr::ungroup() %>% dplyr::filter(ID==isub) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Decision = dplyr::recode(Decision,'More'=1,'Less'=0))
  for (isess in unique(dft$session)){
    for (imod in unique(dft$Modality)){
      df= dft %>% dplyr::filter(session==isess & Modality==imod)
      df.nonScaled = dft.nonScaled %>% dplyr::filter(session==isess & Modality==imod)
     # Separately for each condition
      glms=list()
      glms$dec = glm(Decision~ DV_ResponseMinListen,data=df,family='binomial')
      # Control analyses
      glms$dec.withAvgListenResponseBPM = glm(Decision~ DV_ResponseMinListen+ listen.responseBPM.mean,data=df,family='binomial')
      glms$dec.listenRespBPMsep =         glm(Decision~ listenBPM+responseBPM,data=df,family='binomial')
      glms$dec.soundHeart5trPastsound5tr= glm(Decision~ responseBPM+rollingHeartAvg.5tr+rollingResponseAvg.5tr.prev,data=df,family='binomial')
      glms$dec.soundPastsound5tr=         glm(Decision~ responseBPM+rollingResponseAvg.5tr.prev,data=df,family='binomial')
      glms$dec.soundHeart5tr=             glm(Decision~ responseBPM+rollingHeartAvg.5tr,data=df,family='binomial')
     
      # We're using NA omit to make sure there is the same number of data points for each (this should anyway be the case, it wasnt before when we had yet another model - that did not perform well - that computed DV comparing sound minus average sound of last 5 or so trials)
      df.comparison= df.nonScaled %>% dplyr::select(Decision,DV_ResponseMinListen,responseBPM,easiness_ResponseMinListen.abs) %>% na.omit()
      glms$forLogLik.listenBeep = glm(Decision ~ DV_ResponseMinListen,data=df.comparison,family='binomial')
      glms$forLogLik.responseBeepOnly = glm(Decision ~ responseBPM,data=df.comparison,family='binomial')
      glms$forLogLik.listenBeep.confidence = lm(Confidence ~ easiness_ResponseMinListen.abs,data=df)
      
      results.logLiks=bind_rows(results.logLiks,
                                data.frame(ID=isub,session=isess,Modality=imod,order=df.nonScaled$order[1],
                                           logLik.listenBeep=logLik(glms$forLogLik.listenBeep),
                                           logLik.responseBeepOnly = logLik( glms$forLogLik.responseBeepOnly),
                                           nobs.listenBeep = nobs(glms$forLogLik.listenBeep),
                                           nobs.responseBeepOnly = nobs(glms$forLogLik.responseBeepOnly)))
      
       glms$conf= lm(Confidence ~ easiness_ResponseMinListen.abs,data=df)
       
      for (ireg in names(glms)){
        t=as.data.frame(summary(glms[[ireg]])$coefficients) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column() %>%
          dplyr::mutate(ID=isub,session=isess,Modality=imod,regression=ireg)
        results.indivModalities=bind_rows(results.indivModalities,t)
      }
      # For the plot also without scaling
      df.notscaled= cardio %>%  dplyr::filter(ID==isub & session==isess & Modality==imod) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(Decision = dplyr::recode(Decision,'More'=1,'Less'=0))
      glms.dec.notScaled=list()
      glms.dec.notScaled$dec= glm(Decision~DV_ResponseMinListen,data=df.notscaled,family='binomial')
      glms.dec.notScaled$dec.listenRespBPMsep = glm(Decision~ listenBPM+responseBPM,data=df,family='binomial')
      for (ireg in names(glms.dec.notScaled)){
        t=as.data.frame(summary(glms.dec.notScaled[[ireg]])$coefficients) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column() %>%
          dplyr::mutate(ID=isub,session=isess,Modality=imod,regression=ireg)
        results.indivModalities.notScaled.forPlot = bind_rows(results.indivModalities.notScaled.forPlot,t)
      }
    }
    
  }
}

results.indivModalities=results.indivModalities %>% dplyr::mutate(rowname=dplyr::recode(rowname,`(Intercept)` = 'Intercept')) %>%
  left_join(.,med.data,by='ID')
write.csv(results.indivModalities,file=file.path(paths$base.path,'Data_preprocessed','Interoception_Regression_withinSubjRegression.csv'))
t= results.indivModalities %>% dplyr::filter(regression=='dec') %>% dplyr::select(-`Std. Error`,-`z value`,-`t value`,-`Pr(>|t|)`) %>%
    pivot_wider(.,id_cols=c('ID','rowname','order'),values_from='Estimate',names_from=c('session','Modality')) %>% #'Age','Sex',
    dplyr::mutate(Extero_CDMmNDM = CDM_Extero-NDM_Extero,
                  Intero_CDMmNDM = CDM_Intero-NDM_Intero)
# Write data so it can be read easily into JASP for computing Bayes Factors
write.csv(t %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=="DV_ResponseMinListen"),file=file.path(paths$stats,'Interoception_Regression_withinSubjRegressio_dec_DVResponseMinListen.csv'))
write.csv(t %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=="Intercept")%>%
            dplyr::mutate(Intero_absCDM_m_absNDM=abs(CDM_Intero)-abs(NDM_Intero)),
          file=file.path(paths$stats,'Interoception_Regression_withinSubjRegressio_dec_absIntercept.csv'))
# for JASP: heart rate only 
t= results.indivModalities %>% dplyr::filter(regression=='dec.soundHeart5tr') %>% dplyr::select(-`Std. Error`,-`z value`,-`t value`,-`Pr(>|t|)`) %>%
    pivot_wider(.,id_cols=c('ID','rowname','order'),values_from='Estimate',names_from=c('session','Modality')) %>% #'Age','Sex',
    dplyr::mutate(Extero_CDMmNDM = CDM_Extero-NDM_Extero,
                  Intero_CDMmNDM = CDM_Intero-NDM_Intero,
                  Extero_CDMplusNDM = CDM_Extero+NDM_Extero,
                  Intero_CDMplusNDM = CDM_Intero+NDM_Intero)
write.csv(t %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=="rollingHeartAvg.5tr"),file=file.path(paths$stats,'Interoception_Regression_withinSubjRegressio_decSoundHeart5tr_heartRateReg.csv'))


t= results.indivModalities %>% dplyr::filter(regression=='dec.listenRespBPMsep') %>% dplyr::select(-`Std. Error`,-`z value`,-`t value`,-`Pr(>|t|)`) %>%
    pivot_wider(.,id_cols=c('ID','rowname','order'),values_from='Estimate',names_from=c('session','Modality')) %>% #'Age','Sex',
    dplyr::mutate(Extero_CDMmNDM = CDM_Extero-NDM_Extero,
                  Intero_CDMmNDM = CDM_Intero-NDM_Intero,
                  Extero_CDMplusNDM = CDM_Extero+NDM_Extero,
                  Intero_CDMplusNDM = CDM_Intero+NDM_Intero)
write.csv(t %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=="listenBPM"),file=file.path(paths$stats,'Interoception_Regression_withinSubjRegressio_decListenRespBPMsep_listenBPMieHeart.csv'))

```


##Analyse the regression weights
Bayes factors to be done with JASP.
Here we'll compute for each regressor (including intercept) in each regression (which are again separate for interoception and exteroception):
[1] General measures
- Average value for each intervention (CDM and NDM), as well as t-tests whether regression weights are significant separately in each
- Average values and t-tests across the two sessions (for each person make first the average across CDM and NDM)
[2] Intervention comparisons (CDM minus NDM):
- controlling only for order: reg_weight_CDM_minus_NDM ~ 1 + order [so the intercept here will capture whether there is a difference between CDM and NDM and order whether the difference CDM vs NDM is affected by order of doing CDM or NDM first]
[3] Control analyses: the sessions differed in mean heart rate. And while they did not differ in heartrate SD, we nevertheless also controlled for this
```{r}
session.comparisons=data.frame()

for (itype in unique(results.indivModalities$regression)){ 
# make the difference CDM min NDM
  dft1=results.indivModalities %>% dplyr::filter(regression==itype) %>% dplyr::select(-`Std. Error`,-`z value`,-`t value`,-`Pr(>|t|)`,-'Pr(>|z|)')
  if (itype=='dec.listenRespBPMsep'){ # for this one add a row that combines them
    t = dft1 %>% 
      pivot_wider(.,id_cols=c('ID','order','session','Modality','regression'),values_from='Estimate',names_from='rowname') %>%
      dplyr::mutate(listen_minus_responseBPM_beta = listenBPM-responseBPM) %>% 
      dplyr::select(ID,order,session,Modality,listen_minus_responseBPM_beta,regression) %>%
      pivot_longer(.,cols=c('listen_minus_responseBPM_beta'),names_to='rowname',values_to='Estimate') 
    dft1= bind_rows(dft1,t)  
  }
  dft = dft1 %>%
    pivot_wider(.,id_cols=c('ID','rowname','order'),values_from='Estimate',names_from=c('session','Modality')) %>% #'Age','Sex',
    dplyr::mutate(Extero_CDMmNDM = CDM_Extero-NDM_Extero,
                  Intero_CDMmNDM = CDM_Intero-NDM_Intero,
                  # new:across sessions:
                  Extero_CDMandNDM = (CDM_Extero+NDM_Extero)/2,
                  Intero_CDMandNDM = (CDM_Intero+NDM_Intero)/2)
  
  
  # when itype is dec, let's also test the absolute
  if (stringr::str_detect(itype,'dec')){ 
    t= dft %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='Intercept') %>%
      dplyr::mutate(rowname=dplyr::recode(rowname,Intercept="Intercept.abs"),
                    Intero_CDMmNDM=abs(CDM_Intero)-abs(NDM_Intero),
                    Extero_CDMmNDM=abs(CDM_Extero)-abs(NDM_Extero),
                    Extero_CDMandNDM = (abs(CDM_Extero)+abs(NDM_Extero))/2,
                    Intero_CDMandNDM = (abs(CDM_Intero)+abs(NDM_Intero))/2,
                    CDM_Intero=abs(CDM_Intero),
                    NDM_Intero=abs(NDM_Intero),
                    CDM_Extero=abs(CDM_Extero),
                    NDM_Extero=abs(NDM_Extero))
    dft=bind_rows(dft,t)
  }
  
  for (ibeta in unique(dft$rowname)){
    
    for (imodality in c('Intero','Extero')){
      df = dft %>% dplyr::filter(rowname==ibeta) %>% dplyr::select(order,contains(imodality),ID)
      
      # compute for each of CDM and NDM a t-test against zero (one-sample,two-sided)
      main.effects.p= df %>%  dplyr::select(-contains('CDMmNDM'),-contains('CDMandNDM')) %>%
        pivot_longer(cols=contains(imodality),names_to='session',values_to='value') %>%
        dplyr::group_by(session) %>% dplyr::summarize(p.value.session.mainEffect=t.test(value,mu=0)$p.value) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(rowname=ibeta,Modality=imodality,type=itype) %>% dplyr::select(session,p.value.session.mainEffect) %>%
        pivot_wider(.,names_from=session,values_from=p.value.session.mainEffect,names_prefix = 'p.value.session.mainEffect__') %>%
        # from the column name remove imodality
        dplyr::rename_all(~str_remove(.,imodality))
       main.effects.estimate= df %>%  dplyr::select(-contains('CDMmNDM'),-contains('CDMandNDM')) %>%
        pivot_longer(cols=contains(imodality),names_to='session',values_to='value') %>%
        dplyr::group_by(session) %>% dplyr::summarize(estimate.session.mainEffect=t.test(value,mu=0)$estimate) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(rowname=ibeta,Modality=imodality,type=itype) %>% dplyr::select(session,estimate.session.mainEffect) %>%
        pivot_wider(.,names_from=session,values_from=estimate.session.mainEffect,names_prefix = 'estimate.value.session.mainEffect__') %>%
        # from the column name remove imodality
        dplyr::rename_all(~str_remove(.,imodality))
       main.effects=cbind(main.effects.p,main.effects.estimate)
       
      # also combining both groups
       main.effects.groupsCombined=df %>% dplyr::select(contains('CDMandNDM')) %>%
        pivot_longer(cols=contains(imodality),names_to='session',values_to='value') %>% #dplyr::group_by(session) 
        dplyr::summarize(p.value.bothSessions.mainEffect=t.test(value,mu=0)$p.value,
                         estimate.value.bothSessions.mainEffect=t.test(value,mu=0)$estimate)
      
      # Regressions to test the effect of CDM vs NDM, controllinf for order
      this.lm= lm(formula=paste0(imodality,'_CDMmNDM~ 1+order'),data=df) 
      stats.summary=as.data.frame(summary(this.lm)$coefficients) %>% rownames_to_column(var='group.level.reg') %>% 
        # dplyr::recode group.level.reg (Intercept) with NDM min CDM [!! note 30/5/2025: CDM min NDM, not other wsay round!]
        dplyr::mutate(group.level.reg=dplyr::recode(group.level.reg,`(Intercept)`='CDMminNDM')) %>%   #'NDMminCDM')) %>% 
        pivot_wider(names_from=group.level.reg,values_from=c('Estimate','Std. Error','t value','Pr(>|t|)'),names_sep='__')
      
      # new control analysis - Legrand suggestion: control for heartrate mean
      t= left_join(df,heart.rates.mean.sd %>% dplyr::select(ID,heartRate.mean_cdm_min_ndm),by='ID')
      this.lm= lm(formula=paste0(imodality,'_CDMmNDM~ 1+order+heartRate.mean_cdm_min_ndm'),data=t) 
      stats.summary.controlMeanHR=as.data.frame(summary(this.lm)$coefficients) %>% rownames_to_column(var='group.level.reg') %>% 
        # dplyr::recode group.level.reg (Intercept) with NDM min CDM
        dplyr::mutate(group.level.reg=dplyr::recode(group.level.reg,`(Intercept)`='CDMminNDM')) %>% 
        dplyr::rename(Estimate.CDMmNDM.ctrHRmean=Estimate, 
                      `Std. Error.CDMmNDM.ctrHRmean`=`Std. Error`, 
                      `t value.CDMnNDM.ctrHRmean` = `t value`,
                      `Pr(>|t|).CDMmNDM.ctrHRmean`=`Pr(>|t|)`)
      # The same, but for HR SD
      t= left_join(df,heart.rates.mean.sd %>% dplyr::select(ID,heartRate.sd_cdm_min_ndm),by='ID')
      this.lm= lm(formula=paste0(imodality,'_CDMmNDM~ 1+order+heartRate.sd_cdm_min_ndm'),data=t) 
      stats.summary.controlSDHR=as.data.frame(summary(this.lm)$coefficients) %>% rownames_to_column(var='group.level.reg') %>% 
        # dplyr::recode group.level.reg (Intercept) with NDM min CDM
        dplyr::mutate(group.level.reg=dplyr::recode(group.level.reg,`(Intercept)`='CDMminNDM')) %>% 
        dplyr::rename(Estimate.CDMmNDM.ctrHRsd=Estimate, 
                      `Std. Error.CDMmNDM.ctrHRsd`=`Std. Error`, 
                      `t value.CDMnNDM.ctrHRsd` = `t value`,
                      `Pr(>|t|).CDMmNDM.ctrHRsd`=`Pr(>|t|)`)
     
      # join what we computed above to later print to file
      this.stats.complete= cbind(main.effects,
                                 main.effects.groupsCombined,
                                 stats.summary) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(Modality=imodality,Subject.level.regression.weight=ibeta,analysis.type=itype,
                      heartRate.mean_cdm_min_ndm.estimate=stats.summary.controlMeanHR %>% 
                        dplyr::filter(group.level.reg=="heartRate.mean_cdm_min_ndm") %>% pull(Estimate.CDMmNDM.ctrHRmean),
                      heartRate.mean_cdm_min_ndm.p = stats.summary.controlMeanHR %>% 
                        dplyr::filter(group.level.reg=="heartRate.mean_cdm_min_ndm") %>% pull(`Pr(>|t|).CDMmNDM.ctrHRmean`),
                      CDMmNDM.ctrHRmean.p = stats.summary.controlMeanHR %>% dplyr::filter(group.level.reg=="CDMminNDM") %>% pull(`Pr(>|t|).CDMmNDM.ctrHRmean`),
                      CDMmNDM.ctrHRmean.estimate = stats.summary.controlMeanHR %>% dplyr::filter(group.level.reg=="CDMminNDM") %>% pull(Estimate.CDMmNDM.ctrHRmean),
                      
                      heartRate.sd_cdm_min_ndm.estimate= stats.summary.controlSDHR %>% 
                        dplyr::filter(group.level.reg=="heartRate.sd_cdm_min_ndm") %>% pull(Estimate.CDMmNDM.ctrHRsd),
                      heartRate.sd_cdm_min_ndm.p =  stats.summary.controlSDHR %>% 
                        dplyr::filter(group.level.reg=="heartRate.sd_cdm_min_ndm") %>% pull(`Pr(>|t|).CDMmNDM.ctrHRsd`),
                      CDMmNDM.ctrHRsd.p =  stats.summary.controlSDHR %>% dplyr::filter(group.level.reg=="CDMminNDM") %>% pull(`Pr(>|t|).CDMmNDM.ctrHRsd`),
                      CDMmNDM.ctrHRsd.estimate =  stats.summary.controlSDHR %>% dplyr::filter(group.level.reg=="CDMminNDM") %>% pull(Estimate.CDMmNDM.ctrHRsd))
      session.comparisons=rbind(session.comparisons,this.stats.complete) 
      
      
    }
  }
}

write.csv(session.comparisons,file=file.path(paths$stats,'Interoception_NDMCDMcomparisons_fitSingleSub.csv'))
```

# Figures for the paper
## Decision curves with predictions

We can use the regression weights created above to create a predicted value of % choice for each person for each value (we'll add this to our plot as a line)
```{r}
x=seq(-51,51,1)
predictions=data.frame()
for (isub in unique(results.indivModalities.notScaled.forPlot$ID)){
  for (isess in c('NDM','CDM')){
    for (imod in c('Intero','Extero')){
      pars = results.indivModalities.notScaled.forPlot %>% dplyr::filter(ID==isub & session==isess & regression=='dec' & Modality==imod) %>% 
        dplyr::select(rowname,Estimate) %>%pivot_wider(.,values_from=Estimate,names_from=rowname)
      y = 1/(1+exp(-(pars$`(Intercept)`+x*pars$DV_ResponseMinListen)))
      predictions=rbind(predictions,
                        data.frame(DV_ResponseMinListen=x,perc.choice.predicted=y,ID=isub,session=isess,Modality=imod))
    }
  }
}


```

```{r}
bins = data.frame(low=quantile(c(min(cardio$DV_ResponseMinListen)-0.5,cardio$DV_ResponseMinListen), probs = seq(0,0.9,0.1)), # to make sure we get the edges with the later rules
```

## Regression weights
For decision: 
- Intercept
- absolute intercept
- decision value
For confidence:
- all regression weights (+intercept)
Each split for the two groups. And split for intero/extero. Tim should add the statistics manually (nothing significant).

```{r}

plots=list()
df=results.indivModalities %>% dplyr::filter(regression %in% c('dec','conf')) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(rowname=dplyr::recode(rowname,`(Intercept)` = 'Intercept',
                DV_ResponseMinListen="Stimulus difference",easiness_ResponseMinListen.abs="Stimulus easiness",
                ResponseCorrect="Correct response",DecisionRT="RT (decision)"))
# models with stimulus difference
for (imod in c('Intero','Extero')){
  for (ireg in c('dec','conf')){
    df.this=df %>% dplyr::filter(Modality==imod,regression==ireg)
    if (ireg=='dec'){
      t= df.this %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='Intercept') %>%
        dplyr::mutate(rowname=dplyr::recode(rowname,Intercept="Intercept.abs"),
                      Estimate=abs(Estimate))
      df.this=bind_rows(df.this,t) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(rowname=factor(rowname,ordered=T,levels=c('Stimulus difference','Intercept.abs','Intercept')))
    } else if (ireg=='conf'){
      df.this=df.this %>% dplyr::mutate(rowname=factor(rowname,ordered=T,levels=c('Stimulus easiness','Intercept')))
    }
    # add some jitter so that the points don't completely overlap and become more visible
      jitterVal.abs=0.2
      df.this=df.this%>%dplyr::mutate(jitterVal=case_when(session=='CDM' ~ -jitterVal.abs,
                                                          T ~ jitterVal.abs),
                                      jitterVal=rnorm(nrow(df.this),mean=jitterVal,sd=0.05))
      summaryData = df.this %>%
        group_by(rowname, session) %>%
        summarise(meanEstimate = mean(Estimate)
                  , jitterVal = mean(jitterVal),
                  sdEstimate=sd(Estimate),
                  n=n(),
                  se = sdEstimate/sqrt(n)) %>%
        mutate(xmin = as.numeric(rowname)+jitterVal, 
               xend = as.numeric(rowname)+jitterVal) 
      
      sigData <- df.this %>%
        filter(rowname != "Intercept.abs") %>%  # Exclude Intercept.abs
        group_by(rowname, session) %>%
        summarise(
          p = t.test(Estimate, mu = 0)$p.value,
          ystar = 11 #max(Estimate, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.5
        ) %>%
        mutate(
          star = case_when(
            p < 0.001 ~ "***",
            p < 0.01 ~ "**",
            p < 0.05 ~ "*",
            TRUE ~ ""
          ),
          xstar = as.numeric(rowname) + ifelse(session == "CDM", -0.2, 0.2)
        )


      
      plots[[paste0(imod,'_',ireg)]] = ggplot(df.this, aes(x=as.numeric(rowname)+jitterVal, y=Estimate)) +
        geom_point(size=1, aes(colour=session), alpha=0.7) +
        geom_line(aes(group=interaction(ID, rowname)), alpha=0.3) + # Connect CDM/NDM for each regressor and ID
        scale_colour_manual(values=c('CDM'='blue','NDM'='red')) +
        xlab('Regressor') +
        ggtitle('') +
        scale_x_continuous(
          limits=c(0.5, 3.5),
          breaks=seq(1, length(levels(df.this$rowname)), 1)-0.1,
          labels=levels(df.this$rowname)
        ) +
        ylab('Regression weights') +
        guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1))) +
        geom_point(data=summaryData, size=2, aes(x=xmin, y=meanEstimate, color=session, group=NA)) +
        geom_errorbar(data=summaryData, aes(x=xmin, y=meanEstimate, ymin=meanEstimate-se, ymax=meanEstimate+se, color=session, group=NA)) +
        geom_text(data=sigData, aes(x=xstar, y=ystar, label=star, color=session), size=6, vjust=0,show.legend = FALSE) +
        theme_bw()
      
  }
}

# model with sound and heart rate (or stim 1- stim2)

  scale_x_continuous(

  ) +

  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1))) +
  geom_point(data=summaryData, size=2, aes(x=xmin, y=meanEstimate, color=session, group=NA)) +
  geom_errorbar(data=summaryData, aes(x=xmin, y=meanEstimate, ymin=meanEstimate-se, ymax=meanEstimate+se, color=session, group=NA)) +
  geom_text(data=sigData, aes(x=xstar, y=ystar, label=star, color=session), size=6, vjust=0,show.legend = FALSE) +
  theme_bw()
    
  }
```

```{r}
session.comparisons=read.csv(file.path(paths$stats,'Interoception_NDMCDMcomparisons_fitSingleSub.csv'))
# main text: Intero/Extero, decision/confidence, against zero (CDM and NDM separately), comparing NDM vs CDM (estimate (se.); p-value, BF), order effects
main=session.comparisons %>% 
  dplyr::select(Modality,analysis.type,Subject.level.regression.weight,contains('.mainEffect'),
                Estimate__CDMminNDM,Std..Error__CDMminNDM,Pr...t..__CDMminNDM,Estimate__orderNDM.first,Std..Error__orderNDM.first,Pr...t..__orderNDM.first,
                CDMmNDM.ctrHRmean.p,CDMmNDM.ctrHRsd.p) %>%  #BF.mean.customSD
  dplyr::mutate("CDM min NDM, mean(s.e.)"=paste0(round(Estimate__CDMminNDM,digits=2),' (',round(Std..Error__CDMminNDM,digits=1),')'),
                "CDM min NDM (p)"=case_when(Pr...t..__CDMminNDM<0.01 ~ round(Pr...t..__CDMminNDM,digits=3),    #"NDM vs CDM (p)"
                                T ~ round(Pr...t..__CDMminNDM,digits=2)),
                'CDM minNDM, ctr HR mean (p)' = case_when(CDMmNDM.ctrHRmean.p<0.001 ~ '<0.001',
                                                     CDMmNDM.ctrHRmean.p<0.01 ~ as.character(round(CDMmNDM.ctrHRmean.p,digits=3)),
                                                     T~ as.character(round(CDMmNDM.ctrHRmean.p,digits=2))),
                'CDM minNDM, ctr HR sd (p)' = case_when(CDMmNDM.ctrHRsd.p<0.001 ~ '<0.001',
                                                     CDMmNDM.ctrHRsd.p<0.01 ~ as.character(round(CDMmNDM.ctrHRsd.p,digits=3)),
                                                     T~ as.character(round(CDMmNDM.ctrHRsd.p,digits=2))),
                "Order [NDM first], mean(s.e.)" =paste0(round(Estimate__orderNDM.first,digits=2),' (',round(Std..Error__orderNDM.first,digits=1),')'),
                "Order [NDM first] (p)" = case_when(Pr...t..__orderNDM.first<0.01 ~ round(Pr...t..__orderNDM.first,digits=3),
                                T ~ round(Pr...t..__orderNDM.first,digits=2)),
                p.value.session.mainEffect__CDM_= case_when(p.value.session.mainEffect__CDM_<0.001 ~ '<0.001',
                                                            p.value.session.mainEffect__CDM_<0.01 ~ as.character(round(p.value.session.mainEffect__CDM_,digits=3)),
                                                            T~ as.character(round(p.value.session.mainEffect__CDM_,digits=2))),
                p.value.session.mainEffect__NDM_= case_when(p.value.session.mainEffect__NDM_ < 0.001 ~ '<0.001',
                                                            p.value.session.mainEffect__NDM_<0.01 ~ as.character(round(p.value.session.mainEffect__NDM_,digits=3)),
                                                            T~ as.character(round(p.value.session.mainEffect__NDM_,digits=2))),
                p.value.bothSessions.mainEffect= case_when(p.value.bothSessions.mainEffect<0.001~'<0.001',
                                                           p.value.bothSessions.mainEffect<0.01 ~ as.character(round(p.value.bothSessions.mainEffect,digits=3)),
                                                           T ~  as.character(round(p.value.bothSessions.mainEffect,digits=2))),
                estimate.value.bothSessions.mainEffect  = round(estimate.value.bothSessions.mainEffect,2),
                estimate.value.session.mainEffect__CDM_ = round(estimate.value.session.mainEffect__CDM_,2),
                estimate.value.session.mainEffect__NDM_ = round(estimate.value.session.mainEffect__NDM_,2)) %>%
  dplyr::rename("CDM (p, one-sample)"=p.value.session.mainEffect__CDM_,
                "NDM (p, one-sample)"=p.value.session.mainEffect__NDM_,
                'CDM&NDM (p,one-sample)'=p.value.bothSessions.mainEffect,
                'CDM&NDM (estimate)'=estimate.value.bothSessions.mainEffect,
                'CDM (estimate)' = estimate.value.session.mainEffect__CDM_,
                'NDM (estimate)' = estimate.value.session.mainEffect__NDM_)%>%
  dplyr::select(-contains('Pr...'),-contains('Estimate__'),-contains('Std..Error'),-contains('p.value.session.main'),-contains('ctrHR')) %>% #,-BF.mean.customSD) %>%
  # sort the data frame frist by Modality, then by analysis.type, then by Subject.level.regression.weight
  dplyr::arrange(desc(Modality)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Subject.level.regression.weight=case_when(Modality=='Intero' ~ dplyr::recode(Subject.level.regression.weight,
                                                       DV_ResponseMinListen="Stimulus difference (Sound-Heart)",
                                                       easiness_ResponseMinListen.abs="Stimulus easiness",
                                                       ResponseCorrect="Correct response",
                                                       DecisionRT="RT (decision)",
                                                       listen.responseBPM.mean="Sound+Heart",
                                                       Intercept.abs='Absolute of intercept',
                                                       listenBPM='Heart (bpm)',
                                                       responseBPM = 'Sound (bpm)',
                                                       listen_minus_responseBPM_beta='Regr. weight diff (Sound minus Heart)'),
                                                     Modality=='Extero' ~ dplyr::recode(Subject.level.regression.weight,
                                                       DV_ResponseMinListen="Stimulus difference (Sound2-Sound1)",
                                                       easiness_ResponseMinListen.abs="Stimulus easiness",
                                                       ResponseCorrect="Correct response",
                                                       DecisionRT="RT (decision)",
                                                       listen.responseBPM.mean="Sound1+Sound2",
                                                       Intercept.abs='Absolute of intercept',
                                                       listenBPM='Sound 1 (bpm)',
```

# Control analysis: hierarchical regression
## Meditation data
One surprsing result above was that when including sound and heart rate separately, for interoception there seems to be a CDM vs NDM difference for the sound, but this is not reflected in the exteroception condition, which suggests to me a false postive finding. We'll repeat the regressions as hierarchical.

In conclusion, we'll have the following equations for the task parameters:
- DV
- DV + mean(listen+reponseBPM)
- listenBPM + reponseBPM

For the session measures, we have:
- (session+session_time) [i.e. session type - CDM or NDM - and session time - session 1 or session 2]
- (session*session_time)
- (session*order) [order is a between-subject factor only as each person only has done one order]

Print summary tables.
- all results from (session+session_time) 
- for the others: only the rows with interaction terms
Consider swapping dimensions to put more on the same

New 19/6/2025: last 5 trials average heart rate.
Here it looks like it's significant, but I had somehow in mind that this depended on the standardization? NOPE, see below.
19/9/2025: modified the code to run the data either scaled WITHIN person (and session) or BETWEEN person (i.e. removing grouping and then across the whole data). Turns out to be significant for both types of z-scoring. I am not sure why this was not significant in the non-hierarchical models as 50 trials per person should usually be significant (other difference: BRMS vs standard optimizer).
It turns out that in fact the past heart rate is NOT significant. This aligns more with what we'd seen in the non-hierarchical models. 
Given this, for the write up, we will just omit these analyses.

```{r}
overwrite=F
df.scaled.across= cardio %>% dplyr::filter(Modality=='Intero') %>%
  dplyr::mutate(session_time = case_when(session=='CDM' &order=='CDM.first' ~ 'session1',
                                         session=='CDM' &order=='NDM.first' ~ 'session2',
                                         session=='NDM' &order=='CDM.first' ~ 'session2',
                                         session=='NDM' &order=='NDM.first' ~ 'session1'),
                Decision.num = case_when(Decision=='More' ~1,
                                         Decision=='Less' ~ 0)) %>%
  dplyr::select(ID,Decision,Decision.num,DV_ResponseMinListen,session,session_time,listenBPM,responseBPM,listen.responseBPM.mean,order, rollingHeartAvg.5tr,rollingResponseAvg.5tr.prev,rollingResponseAvg.1tr.prev,rollingResponseAvg.3tr.prev) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate_at(c('DV_ResponseMinListen','listenBPM','responseBPM','listen.responseBPM.mean','rollingHeartAvg.5tr','rollingResponseAvg.5tr.prev','rollingResponseAvg.1tr.prev','rollingResponseAvg.3tr.prev'),scale)
df.scaled.within= cardio %>% dplyr::filter(Modality=='Intero') %>%
  dplyr::mutate(session_time = case_when(session=='CDM' &order=='CDM.first' ~ 'session1',
                                         session=='CDM' &order=='NDM.first' ~ 'session2',
                                         session=='NDM' &order=='CDM.first' ~ 'session2',
                                         session=='NDM' &order=='NDM.first' ~ 'session1'),
                Decision.num = case_when(Decision=='More' ~1,
                                         Decision=='Less' ~ 0)) %>%
  dplyr::select(ID,Decision,Decision.num,DV_ResponseMinListen,session,session_time,listenBPM,responseBPM,listen.responseBPM.mean,order, rollingHeartAvg.5tr,rollingResponseAvg.5tr.prev,rollingResponseAvg.1tr.prev,rollingResponseAvg.3tr.prev) %>%
  group_by(ID,session) %>%
  dplyr::mutate_at(c('DV_ResponseMinListen','listenBPM','responseBPM','listen.responseBPM.mean','rollingHeartAvg.5tr','rollingResponseAvg.5tr.prev','rollingResponseAvg.1tr.prev','rollingResponseAvg.3tr.prev'),scale)

my.prior=c(prior(normal(0,3),class='b')) 

formulas.basic= c('(listenBPM+responseBPM)',
                  #'(DV_ResponseMinListen+listen.responseBPM.mean)',
                  #'DV_ResponseMinListen',
                  '(rollingHeartAvg.5tr+responseBPM)',
                  '(rollingHeartAvg.5tr+responseBPM+rollingResponseAvg.5tr.prev)',
                  '(rollingHeartAvg.5tr+responseBPM+rollingResponseAvg.1tr.prev)', # to check whether 5 trials gets close to the average
                  '(rollingHeartAvg.5tr+responseBPM+rollingResponseAvg.3tr.prev)',
                  '(responseBPM+rollingResponseAvg.5tr.prev)')
formulas.conditions = c('*(session+session_time)',
                        '*(session+order)')
 # '*(session*session_time)',
                        # '*(session*order)',

model.count=0;
for (ibasic in formulas.basic){
  for (icond in formulas.conditions){
    for (izscore in c('zscoreWithin','zscoreAcrossonly')){
    model.count=model.count+1
    this.file=file.path(paths$stats,paste0('Hierarchical_Interoception_model',ibasic,'__',icond,'_',izscore,'.csv')) #model.count,'.csv'))
    this.file.long=file.path(paths$stats,paste0('Hierarchical_Interoception_model',ibasic,'__',icond,'_',izscore,'_check.txt'))
    if (!file.exists(this.file)| overwrite==T){
      if (icond=='*(session+order)') {
        this.formula= paste0('Decision.num ~',ibasic,icond,'+ (',ibasic,'*session|ID)')
      } else{
        this.formula= paste0('Decision.num ~',ibasic,icond,'+ (',ibasic,icond,'|ID)')
      }
      
      print(this.formula)
      if (izscore=='zscoreWithin'){
        df = df.scaled.within
      } else{
        df= df.scaled.across
      }
      print(paste('Fitting basic',ibasic,'condition',icond,'zscore',izscore))
      fit = brm(this.formula,
                data=df,family=bernoulli(link='logit'),prior=my.prior,iter=8000,control=list(adapt_delta =0.9))
      write.csv(as.data.frame(fixef(fit)) %>% dplyr::mutate_if(is.numeric,~round(.,2)),this.file)
      sink(this.file.long)
      print(summary(fit))
      sink()
    }
    }
  }
}
```

## Reinforcement learning model
I've made the code in SingleSub_Sound_PastSounds_PastHeart. But, this is not checked for whether it works because the regresions above suggested that in fact, there is no evidence that people use the past heart rate. There was an error that I was not separating between modalities and the past heart rate regressor contained in fact past sounds.

# Control analysis: task difficulty over time
Due to the adaptive staircasing procedure, task difficulty might be different across participants, so this might be problematic for regressions, especially when the data is z-scored within each person! (this is why we did not z-score within each person in the analyses above).

But jsut in case, here we check the value the task converges to. 
```{r}
df= cardio %>% dplyr::filter(Modality=='Intero') %>% dplyr::group_by(ID,session,order) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ntr = row_number()) %>% 
  dplyr::filter(ntr>= max(ntr)-4)  %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mean.DV_ResponseMinListen = mean(DV_ResponseMinListen,na.rm=T)) %>% ungroup() %>%
  pivot_wider(.,names_from='session',values_from='mean.DV_ResponseMinListen') %>%
  dplyr::mutate(mean.DV_CDMminNDM = CDM-NDM,
                mean.DV_CDMminNDM.abs = abs(CDM)-abs(NDM))


fit=brm(mean.DV_CDMminNDM.abs~order,data=df)
fit.lm=lm(mean.DV_CDMminNDM.abs~order,data=df)

fit2=brm(mean.DV_CDMminNDM~order,data=df)
fit2.lm=lm(mean.DV_CDMminNDM~order,data=df)
```

# Control analysis: analysing the original Legrand data
```{r}
# Compute variables
cardio.legrand.this = cardio.legrand %>% dplyr::group_by(ID,Modality)  %>%
  dplyr::mutate(DV_ResponseMinListen = responseBPM-listenBPM,
                Decision = dplyr::recode(Decision,'More'=1,'Less'=0)) %>% dplyr::ungroup() 
# run regressions
results.indivModalities.legrand=data.frame()
results.logLiks.glms.legrand = data.frame()

for (isub in unique(cardio.legrand.this$ID)){
  for (imod in unique(cardio.legrand.this$Modality)){
    df= cardio.legrand.this %>% dplyr::filter( Modality==imod & ID==isub)
    
    glms=list()
    glms$dec = glm(Decision~ DV_ResponseMinListen,data=df,family='binomial')
    # Control analyses
    glms$dec.listenRespBPMsep = glm(Decision~ listenBPM+responseBPM,data=df,family='binomial')
    df.comparison= df %>% dplyr::select(Decision,DV_ResponseMinListen,responseBPM) %>% na.omit()
    glms$forLogLik.listenBeep = glm(Decision ~ DV_ResponseMinListen,data=df.comparison,family='binomial')
    glms$forLogLik.responseBeepOnly = glm(Decision ~ responseBPM,data=df.comparison,family='binomial')
    
    results.logLiks.glms.legrand=bind_rows(results.logLiks.glms.legrand,
                                           data.frame(ID=isub,Modality=imod,
                                                      #logLik.avgBeep5tr=logLik(glms$forLogLik.avgBeep5tr),
                                                      logLik.listenBeep=logLik(glms$forLogLik.listenBeep),
                                                      logLik.responseBeepOnly = logLik( glms$forLogLik.responseBeepOnly),
                                                      nobs.listenBeep = nobs(glms$forLogLik.listenBeep),
                                                      nobs.responseBeepOnly = nobs(glms$forLogLik.responseBeepOnly)))
    
    for (ireg in names(glms)){
        t=as.data.frame(summary(glms[[ireg]])$coefficients) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column() %>%
          dplyr::mutate(ID=isub,Modality=imod,regression=ireg)
        results.indivModalities.legrand=bind_rows(results.indivModalities.legrand,t)
      }
  }
}

```

# Simulations
The goal is to see whether we could have measured a heart rate effect in regressions. What we'll do for this:
- Using the non-zscored data from Legrand, get regression weights for sound (range, mean, std) [check shape of distribution]
- Draw random parameters from the distribution
- Simulate choices for 100 participants
- Fit
- Plot regression weights

!! To: repeat for different numbers of trials. This requires some re-organization of the code. Maybe at a minimum, we could just reduce the number of trials we had for our meditaiton study. Legrand: up to 160, but I'd say about 140 on average. Ours: up to 120, average about 100.

## Fit the original Legrand data
Quick check on the data - n trials
```{r}
n.tr.legrand=gghistogram(cardio.legrand %>% dplyr::filter(Modality=='Intero') %>% group_by(ID) %>% dplyr::summarize(n()) %>% pull(`n()`))
n.tr.meditation=gghistogram(cardio %>% dplyr::filter(Modality=='Intero' & session=='CDM') %>% group_by(ID) %>% dplyr::summarize(n()) %>% pull(`n()`))
cardio %>%  group_by(ID,Modality,session) %>% dplyr::summarize(ntr=n())
cardio.legrand %>% group_by(ID,Modality) %>% dplyr::summarize(ntr=n())
ggarrange(n.tr.legrand,n.tr.meditation)
```


Fit the non-zscored data.
Note: 
- when fitting the Legrand data, some participants had fitting issues, we're skipping them (using tryCatch)
- I demeaned but not z-scored the data. This is to help with the simulations (otherwise the intercept needs to absorbe the mean I think; and then combining different regression weights is trickier and for many simulations choices are always the same)
- we selected 54 trials to have a similar number of trials as in our data
```{r}

results.legrand=data.frame()
this.modality='Intero'
n.trials= 54

skip.first.n= 0 # set to 0 not to skip - tried it out, made no difference

legrand.demeaned= cardio.legrand %>% dplyr::filter(Modality==this.modality) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ID) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(listenBPM=listenBPM-mean(listenBPM),
                responseBPM=responseBPM-mean(responseBPM),
                trial.recount = row_number()) %>%
  dplyr::filter(trial.recount>skip.first.n) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(maxTr=n()) %>%
  # for each ID, select only the first n.trials
  dplyr::filter(trial.recount <= min(n.trials,maxTr)) %>%
  #sample_n(min(n.trials,maxTr)) %>%
  ungroup()
for (isub in unique(cardio.legrand$ID)){
  #print(isub)
  
  df = legrand.demeaned %>% 
    dplyr::filter(ID==isub & Modality==this.modality) %>%
    
    dplyr::mutate(Decision = dplyr::recode(Decision,'More'=1,'Less'=0)) %>%
      dplyr::select(ID,listenBPM,responseBPM,Decision)
  
  this.glm= glm(Decision~ listenBPM+responseBPM,data=df,family='binomial')
  
  #tryCatch({m   <-  glm(y~x, family=binomial)}, warning=function(w) print(i))
  
  this.message='OK'
  tryCatch(
    this.glm<-glm(Decision~ listenBPM+responseBPM,data=df,family='binomial'),
    warning = function(w) {this.message<<-'ERROR'}
  )
  if (this.message!='ERROR'){
    t=as.data.frame(summary(this.glm)$coefficients) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column() %>%
      dplyr::mutate(ID=isub,Modality=this.modality,ntr=nrow(df))
    results.legrand=bind_rows(results.legrand,t)
  } else{
    print(paste('there was a warning, skipping', isub))
  }
  rm(this.message,this.glm,df)
  
}

```


## Functions to make new combinations of regression weights, simulate choices, fit the choices and make plots
Create new combinations of regression weights and then choices
Note: 
- heart rate regressors to be the same range as sound, but other way round
- I've set the intercept to zero because we just want to test whether assuming the heart rate range is the same as sound range, can we measure an effect
[done above! - We're drawing 47 random trials, as that's the minimum in the Legrand data and similar enough to our data.]
- It turned out that with ~200 participants, the correlations were not very stable. So we need to have more.
```{r}
func.simulateRegWeightsChoices = function(selection.type){
  if (selection.type=='allParticipants'){
    Intercept.t=results.legrand %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='(Intercept)') %>% pull(Estimate)
    sound.t=results.legrand %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='responseBPM') %>% pull(Estimate)
    heart.t=-(results.legrand %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='responseBPM') %>% pull(Estimate)) # flipped
    ID.t=results.legrand %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='responseBPM') %>% pull(ID)
  } else if (selection.type=='onlyHeartRightDirection'){
    heartGood.IDs = results.legrand %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='listenBPM' & Estimate<0) %>% pull(ID)
    Intercept.t=results.legrand %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='(Intercept)' & ID %in% heartGood.IDs) %>% pull(Estimate)
    sound.t=results.legrand %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='responseBPM' & ID %in% heartGood.IDs) %>% pull(Estimate)
    heart.t=results.legrand %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='listenBPM' & ID %in% heartGood.IDs) %>% pull(Estimate) # good participants
    ID.t=results.legrand %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='responseBPM' & ID %in% heartGood.IDs) %>% pull(ID)
  }
  
  
  
  n.rep.simuls = 10 # to get 2000 in total 
  simul.regs=data.frame()
  for (irep.simul in 1:n.rep.simuls){
    simul.regst = data.frame(ID=ID.t[sample(1:length(ID.t),replace=F)],
                             Intercept=0, #Intercept.t[sample(1:length(Intercept.t),replace=T)],
                             sound=sound.t[sample(1:length(sound.t),replace=F)],
                             heart=heart.t[sample(1:length(heart.t),replace=F)],
                             simul=irep.simul)
    simul.regs = rbind(simul.regs,simul.regst)
  }
  
  simul.choices = data.frame()
  for (isimul in unique(simul.regs$simul)){
    for (isub in unique(simul.regs$ID)){
      # print(isub)
      df = legrand.demeaned %>% 
        dplyr::filter( ID==isub) %>% 
        dplyr::select(listenBPM,responseBPM,ID) 
      
      
      this.sub.regs = simul.regs %>% dplyr::filter(ID==isub & simul==isimul)
      df= df %>% dplyr::mutate(lin.pred = this.sub.regs$Intercept + this.sub.regs$sound*responseBPM + this.sub.regs$heart*listenBPM,
                               pMore = 1/(1+exp(-lin.pred)),
                               Decision.simul= runif(nrow(df),min=0,max=1) < pMore,
                               #Decision.simul = rbinom(n=1,size=1,prob=pMore),
                               simul=isimul)
      simul.choices= bind_rows(simul.choices,df %>% dplyr::select(ID,listenBPM,responseBPM,pMore,Decision.simul,simul))
    }
  }
  out=list()
  out$simul.choices = simul.choices
  out$simul.regs = simul.regs
  return(out)
}

```

Fit the simulations
```{r}
func.fitSimul=function(simul.choices){
simul.fits=data.frame()
for (isimul  in unique(simul.choices$simul)){
for (isub in unique(simul.choices$ID)){
  
  this.modality='Intero'
  df = simul.choices %>% 
    dplyr::filter(ID==isub& simul==isimul ) %>% 
    dplyr::rename(Decision = Decision.simul)
  
  this.glm= glm(Decision~ listenBPM+responseBPM,data=df,family='binomial')
  
  #tryCatch({m   <-  glm(y~x, family=binomial)}, warning=function(w) print(i))
  
  this.message='OK'
  tryCatch(
    this.glm<-glm(Decision~ listenBPM+responseBPM,data=df,family='binomial'),
    warning = function(w) {this.message<<-'ERROR'}
  )
  if (this.message!='ERROR'){
    t=as.data.frame(summary(this.glm)$coefficients) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column() %>%
      dplyr::mutate(ID=isub,Modality=this.modality,simul=isimul)
    simul.fits=bind_rows(simul.fits,t)
  } else{
    print(paste('there was a warning, skipping', isub))
  }
  rm(this.message,this.glm,df)
  
}
}

simul.fits.wide= simul.fits  %>% dplyr::select(ID,simul,rowname,Estimate) %>% 
    dplyr::filter(rowname %in% c('listenBPM','responseBPM')) %>% dplyr::mutate(rowname=dplyr::recode(rowname,'listenBPM'='heart.fit','responseBPM'='sound.fit')) %>%
    pivot_wider(.,id_cols=c('ID','simul'),names_from='rowname',values_from='Estimate')
out=list()
out$simul.fits=simul.fits
out$simul.fits.wide=simul.fits.wide
return(out)
}
```

Plot the results
I've done correlations as that's what you usually do for parameter recovery. But here, we rather want to know whether the group level was significant. 
So what we can do is take x times samples of say 20 participants, and check the significance (and direction) of the simulated and fitted parameters

out.plots.sameEffectHeartSound=func.plotSimulationResults(out.fits$simul.fits.wide,out.regs$simul.regs,out.fits$simul.choices)


```{r}
func.plotSimulationResults=function(simul.fits.wide,simul.regs,simul.choices){
  t=left_join(simul.fits.wide,simul.regs %>% dplyr::rename(sound.simul=sound,heart.simul=heart),by=c('ID','simul'))
  # Correlations
  
  plot.heart=ggscatter(t,x='heart.simul',y='heart.fit',add = 'reg.line',cor.coef=T,xlab='Simulated',ylab='Fitted',title='Ai Heart')
  plot.sound=ggscatter(t,x='sound.simul',y='sound.fit',add = 'reg.line',cor.coef=T,xlab='Simulated',ylab='Fitted',title='Aii Sound')
  plot.tog=ggarrange(plot.heart,plot.sound,nrow=1)
  
  # Main effects 
  nrep= 500
  sample.size=20
  results.subsets=data.frame()
  for (irep in 1:nrep){
    
    selection=simul.fits.wide %>% dplyr::slice_sample(n=sample.size)
    
    
    tog=left_join(selection,simul.regs %>% 
                    dplyr::rename(heart.simul=heart,sound.simul=sound) %>%
                    dplyr::select(-Intercept),
                  by=c('ID','simul')) %>%
      # now with new shuffling doesnt make sense for simul
      dplyr::select(-heart.simul,-sound.simul)
    # t-test on each column
    t= tog %>% pivot_longer(cols=c('heart.fit','sound.fit'),names_to='type',values_to='Estimate') %>%
      dplyr::group_by(type) %>%
      dplyr::summarize(meanEstimate=mean(Estimate),
                       sdEstimate=sd(Estimate),
                       n=n(),
                       se=sdEstimate/sqrt(n),
                       p.value=t.test(Estimate,mu=0)$p.value,
                       p.wilcox=wilcox.test(Estimate,mu=0)$p.value,
                       estimate=t.test(Estimate,mu=0)$estimate) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(rep=irep)
    results.subsets=bind_rows(results.subsets,t)
  }
  # counts
  summary.significantCounts=results.subsets %>%
    dplyr::group_by(type) %>%
    dplyr::summarize(count.sig=sum(p.value<0.05),
                     count.sig.wilcox=sum(p.wilcox<0.05),
                     prop.sig = mean(p.value<0.05),
                     prop.sig.wilcox = mean(p.wilcox<0.05))
  
  # let's also check original range of heart rates
  range = simul.choices  %>%
    dplyr::group_by(ID) %>%
    dplyr::summarize(minHR=min(listenBPM,na.rm=T),
                     maxHR=max(listenBPM,na.rm=T),
                     meanHR=mean(listenBPM,na.rm=T),
                     sdHR=sd(listenBPM,na.rm=T),
                     rangeHR=maxHR-minHR,
                     # the same for sound
                     minSound=min(responseBPM,na.rm=T),
                     maxSound=max(responseBPM,na.rm=T),
                     meanSound=mean(responseBPM,na.rm=T),
                     sdSound=sd(responseBPM,na.rm=T),
                     rangeSound=maxSound-minSound) 
  
  # let's check the HR range against the parameters
  paras.HR = left_join(simul.fits.wide, range,by='ID')
  tab_corr(paras.HR %>% dplyr::select_if(is.numeric) ) 
  
  # Plot results.subsets for type==heart.fit, column  p.value, add a vertical line at 0.05
  plot.results.subsets=gghistogram(results.subsets %>% dplyr::filter(type=='heart.fit'),
                                   x='p.value',ylab='Number of simulation sets of n=20',xlab='p-value', 
                                   title='B Group (n=20) simulated effect significance')+
    geom_vline(xintercept=0.05,linetype='dashed',color='red')
  
  
  # Combine the plots
  plot.supplement.simulation=ggarrange(plot.tog,plot.results.subsets,nrow=2,
                                       common.legend=F,
                                       # left align the labels
                                       hjust=0)
  
  out=list()
  out$summary.significantCounts= summary.significantCounts
  out$plot.supplement.simulation= plot.supplement.simulation
  return(out)
}
```


## Run for different simulation settings
Simulating from participants that have the regression weights in the right direction suggest that in fact if it should be possible to select people who can do the task well and then have them perform it again. with 20 participants, 84% of the time, the group level effect would be significnat again. We can then test it in the legrand data: selecting participants at time one who can do the task, and then make them do it again at time 2.
```{r}
# [1] Assume that the size of the effect is the same for heart and sound
out.regs=func.simulateRegWeightsChoices('allParticipants')
out.fits=func.fitSimul(out.regs$simul.choices)
out.plots.sameEffectHeartSound=func.plotSimulationResults(out.fits$simul.fits.wide,out.regs$simul.regs,out.regs$simul.choices)
ggexport(out.plots.sameEffectHeartSound$plot.supplement.simulation,
         filename=file.path(paths$figures,'Supplements_simulation_sameEffectHeartSound.tiff'),
         width=8*300,height=8*300,res=300)

# [2] Assume every participant with the heart rate effect in the right direction does the task again (But regression weights shuffled)
out.regs=func.simulateRegWeightsChoices('onlyHeartRightDirection')
out.fits=func.fitSimul(out.regs$simul.choices)
out.plots.onlySignifHeartSimul=func.plotSimulationResults(out.fits$simul.fits.wide,out.regs$simul.regs,out.regs$simul.choices)
ggexport(out.plots.onlySignifHeartSimul$plot.supplement.simulation,
         filename=file.path(paths$figures,'Supplements_simulation_heartSensitiveParticipantsOnly.tiff'),
         width=8*300,height=8*300,res=300)
```

# Legrand 
The results are pretty intersting: while in session 1, participants cannot do the task (no significant effect of heart rate), they can in session 2. And there is potentially an effect that participants who could do it in session 1 are also more likely to be able to do it in session 2. Though this does not hold up in the other direction. To fully explain all of this in the present paper would be too much. We have therefore not included it. It is also well possible that Micah Allen and colleagues would prefer to do and publish these analyses themselves (potentially with their new modeling that has some extra features). 

##- test-retest (ish)


```{r}

func.fitLegrandForRetest= function(input){
  results.legrand=data.frame()
  this.modality='Intero'
  #n.trials= 54
  
#  skip.first.n= 0 # set to 0 not to skip - tried it out, made no difference
  # use all trials
  legrand.demeaned= input %>% dplyr::filter(Modality==this.modality) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(ID) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(listenBPM=listenBPM-mean(listenBPM),
                  responseBPM=responseBPM-mean(responseBPM),
                  trial.recount = row_number()) %>%
    dplyr::filter(trial.recount>skip.first.n) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(maxTr=n()) %>%

    ungroup()
  for (isub in unique(input$ID)){
    #print(isub)
    
    df = legrand.demeaned %>% 
      dplyr::filter(ID==isub & Modality==this.modality) %>%
      
      dplyr::mutate(Decision = dplyr::recode(Decision,'More'=1,'Less'=0)) %>%
      dplyr::select(ID,listenBPM,responseBPM,Decision)
    
    this.glm= glm(Decision~ listenBPM+responseBPM,data=df,family='binomial')
    
    #tryCatch({m   <-  glm(y~x, family=binomial)}, warning=function(w) print(i))
    
    this.message='OK'
    tryCatch(
      this.glm<-glm(Decision~ listenBPM+responseBPM,data=df,family='binomial'),
      warning = function(w) {this.message<<-'ERROR'}
    )
    if (this.message!='ERROR'){
      t=as.data.frame(summary(this.glm)$coefficients) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column() %>%
        dplyr::mutate(ID=isub,Modality=this.modality,ntr=nrow(df))
      results.legrand=bind_rows(results.legrand,t)
    } else{
      print(paste('there was a warning, skipping', isub))
    }
    rm(this.message,this.glm,df)
    
  }
  return(results.legrand)
}

```

```{r}
results.legrand.day1= func.fitLegrandForRetest(cardio.legrand)
results.legrand.day2= func.fitLegrandForRetest(cardio.legrand.session2)

comb=left_join(results.legrand.day2 %>% dplyr::select(ID,rowname,Estimate) %>% dplyr::rename(regwday2=Estimate),
               results.legrand.day1 %>% dplyr::select(ID,rowname,Estimate) %>% dplyr::rename(regwday1=Estimate),
               by=c('ID','rowname'))

tab_corr(comb %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='responseBPM') %>% dplyr::select_if(is.numeric))

t.test(comb %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='responseBPM') %>% pull(regwday2))

t.test(comb %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='listenBPM') %>% pull(regwday1))
# How many participants can do the task (negative regression weights for listen, positive for sound) on both days
nrow(comb %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='listenBPM' & regwday2<0 & regwday1<0))/(length(unique(comb$ID)))
nrow(comb %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='listenBPM' & regwday1<0))/(length(unique(comb$ID)))

t.response=comb %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='responseBPM' & regwday2>0 & regwday1>0)
length(intersect(t.listen$ID,t.response$ID))/(length(unique(comb$ID)))

            xlab='Day 1 regression weight (heart rate)',ylab='Day 2 reg weight')+

# Overall improvement day 1 vs day 2?
t=comb %>%

t.test(t %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='listenBPM') %>% pull(improvement))
t.test(t %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='responseBPM') %>% pull(improvement))




# As a control analysis: participants with reversed regression weights should be noise (?)
t.test(comb %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='listenBPM' & regwday1>0) %>% pull(regwday2))

nrow(comb %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='listenBPM' & regwday2<0 & regwday1<0))
nrow(comb %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='listenBPM' & regwday1<0))
nrow(comb %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='listenBPM' & regwday2<0 & regwday1<0))/
  nrow(comb %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='listenBPM' & regwday1<0))

heart.rates.mean.sd.legrand1= cardio.legrand %>%
```

## Curves for heart rate and sound (hierarchical regression)
```{r}
fits=list()
plots=list()
for (isession in c('session1','session2')){
  if (isession=='session1'){
    legrand.this=cardio.legrand
  } else{
    legrand.this = cardio.legrand.session2
  }
  df.scaled.within.legrand= legrand.this %>% dplyr::filter(Modality=='Intero') %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Decision.num = case_when(Decision=='More' ~1,
                                           Decision=='Less' ~ 0)) %>%
    dplyr::select(ID,Decision.num,listenBPM,responseBPM) %>%
    group_by(ID) %>%
    dplyr::mutate_at(c('listenBPM','responseBPM'),scale) %>%
    dplyr::rename('heartBPM'='listenBPM','soundBPM'='responseBPM')
  
  my.prior=c(prior(normal(0,3),class='b')) 
  
  fits[[isession]]=brm(Decision.num ~ (heartBPM + soundBPM) + ((heartBPM + soundBPM)|ID),
                       data=df.scaled.within.legrand,family=bernoulli(link='logit'),prior=my.prior)
  
  p=conditional_effects(fits[[isession]],effects=c('soundBPM','heartBPM'))
  
  plots[[paste0("sound.legrand.",isession)]]=plot(p,points = F, plot = F)[[1]]+theme_bw()+
    ylab('Probability judge sound faster')+xlab('Sound rate (BPM)')
  plots[[paste0("heart.legrand.",isession)]]=plot(p,points = F, plot = F)[[2]]+theme_bw()+
    ylab('Probability judge sound faster')+xlab('Heart rate (BPM)')
}




plots.sound_heartRate.legrand=ggarrange(plots$sound.legrand.session1, plots$heart.legrand.session1,
                                        plots$sound.legrand.session2, plots$heart.legrand.session2, 
                                        nrow=2,ncol=2,
                                        labels = c('A Sound session 1','B Heart rate session 1',
                                                   'C Sound session 2','D Heart rate session 2'))
ggexport(plots.sound_heartRate.legrand,
         filename=file.path(paths$figures,'Supplements_Legrand_ConditionalEffects_heartAndSound_session1_session2.tiff'),
         width=10*300,height=8*300,res=300)

# print the results of the fits (tables to file)

capture.output(summary(fits$session2),file=file.path(paths$stats,'Legrand_HierarchicalRegression_ConditionalEffects_heartAndSound_session2.txt'))
```
